description: Overly Permissive IAM Roles The Lambda execution role combines multiple broad permissions including AWSLakeFormationDataAdmin and AmazonAthenaFullAccess, along with extensive QuickSight permissions. If compromised, an attacker could access and modify sensitive security data across multiple services. An attacker who compromises a Lambda function could leverage the broad permissions to access sensitive data in Lake Formation, modify QuickSight dashboards, or manipulate Athena queries to extract or tamper with security insights data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1548 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
recommendation: Implement fine-grained IAM roles following the principle of least privilege

description: Insecure OpenSearch Domain Configuration The OpenSearch domain uses a master user role with root principal as the assumed role, and the security group configuration is not explicitly defined in terms of inbound rules. If the security group is misconfigured, unauthorized users within the VPC could access the OpenSearch domain. Additionally, the master user credentials, if compromised, would provide full administrative access to the domain.
references: recommendation: Implement strict security group rules
recommendation: Implement IAM-based fine-grained access control

description: Insufficient Data Protection Controls The S3 buckets are configured with RemovalPolicy.DESTROY and autoDeleteObjects: true, which could lead to accidental or malicious deletion of security-critical data. An attacker with access to the AWS account could destroy critical security data by deleting the CloudFormation stack, or an administrator could accidentally delete important audit trails during environment cleanup.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement proper S3 bucket retention controls
recommendation: Implement S3 object lock and versioning
